key_headlines.title: Government Launches Price Stabilization Campaign with Third Oil Price Cap Starting April 10
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul announced the third oil price ceiling effective from April 10, along with comprehensive measures to control consumer prices including subsidies for PCs, telecommunications cost reductions, and controlled food prices.

key_headlines.title: January-February Fiscal Deficit Reaches 14 Trillion Won; National Debt Increases 44 Trillion Won in Two Months
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's cumulative fiscal deficit for January-February reached 14 trillion won, while national debt surged by 44 trillion won, with the debt-to-GDP ratio reaching 49% and expected to exceed 50% with supplementary budget included.

key_headlines.title: Foreign Investors Flee Korean Stock Market with 36.5 Billion Dollar Net Outflow in March; Won Exchange Rate Surges
key_headlines.summary: Foreign investors executed massive sell-offs from the Korean stock market with 36.5 billion dollars in net outflows during March, contributing to sharp increases in the won-dollar exchange rate amid global market uncertainties.

key_headlines.title: K-Battery Makers' Market Share Drops to 30% Range; Technology Competitiveness Critical for Recovery
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's three major battery manufacturers saw their global market share decline to the 30% range due to intensifying price competition and Chinese dominance, requiring renewed focus on technological differentiation.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Apartment Prices Show Mixed Signals; Gangnam Region Declines While Outer Areas Rise
key_headlines.summary: Seoul apartment price increases moderated to 0.10% in the first week of April, with outer regions maintaining upward momentum while Gangnam areas continued declining, indicating divergent market trends by district.

sections.Hot Economy News: The government has launched an all-out price stabilization campaign amid persistent inflationary pressures exacerbated by Middle East tensions. Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul announced the third oil price ceiling effective April 10 and unveiled comprehensive measures including PC subsidies for low-income households, telecommunications bill reductions of over 380 billion won, enhanced hagwon (private academy) fee monitoring, and strategic food supply releases. Without price ceiling policies, March inflation would have risen 2.8% instead of the lower actual rate. The government is releasing government-held mackerel reserves from April 13 through June 30 and providing subsidies for chicken (up to 40% discount) and additional garlic supplies to stabilize food prices.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's fiscal situation deteriorated significantly in the first two months of 2026, with a combined deficit of 14 trillion won, though improved by 4 trillion won compared to the same period last year due to increased tax revenues. National tax revenue increased 10 trillion won to 71 trillion won, driven by gains in income tax (2.4 trillion won), value-added tax (4.1 trillion won), and securities transaction tax (1.2 trillion won from surging stock market activity). However, national debt ballooned by 44 trillion won in just two months, reaching levels that put the debt-to-GDP ratio at 49%, with projections for it to exceed 50% once supplementary budgets are factored in. Total government expenditure reached 128.7 trillion won, up 12 trillion won year-over-year, indicating sustained fiscal pressure.
sections.Financial Markets: Korean stock markets declined with the KOSPI retreating below the 5,800 level amid mixed global signals and foreign investor capital flight. Foreign investors executed net sales of 249.7 billion won, continuing a massive March outflow of 36.5 billion dollars that pushed the won-dollar exchange rate higher. The FOMC meeting minutes indicated Fed officials broadly agreed on rate maintenance for the near term, though geopolitical concerns and inflation risks from Middle East tensions tempered expectations for near-term rate cuts. Sector performance was mixed, with telecommunications and chemicals gaining ground while insurance and construction declined, reflecting cautious market sentiment despite the announced US-Iran ceasefire.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's battery industry faces mounting challenges as major domestic manufacturers' global market share declined to the 30% range amid intensifying competition from Chinese rivals and pressure from major automakers demanding lower prices. The industry is exploring next-generation solutions including sodium-ion batteries set to debut next year to avoid repeating mistakes made with LFP (lithium iron phosphate) technology. Critical supply chains for semiconductors, automobiles, batteries, and shipbuilding remain stable, though some items like paint and packaging materials face supply constraints. The government continues monitoring Hormuz strait passage fee impacts, with potential 0.5% upward pressure on domestic oil prices if such fees become implemented.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment prices showed signs of momentum loss in early April with gains moderating to 0.10%, after several weeks of accelerating increases, with outer districts beginning to show weaker upward pressure. Gangnam and surrounding affluent areas continued their downward trajectory in both purchase and jeonse (long-term lease) markets, while outer areas maintained modest gains. Competition for prime properties remained intense, with the Acro de Seocho redevelopment project recording historic 1,099:1 subscription competition and marking the year's first perfect qualifying score of 84 points. The HUG housing program expanded its affordable jeonse offerings with properties at approximately 90% of market rates and zero real estate commissions, attracting significant demand with a 74:1 competition ratio over two years.
sections.International Economy: The US-Iran ceasefire announced on April 8 provides temporary relief from escalating Middle East tensions that had driven oil prices higher and created significant market volatility. The two-week ceasefire is expected to facilitate initial peace negotiations scheduled for April 11 in Pakistan, though market participants remain cautious about the sustainability of the agreement. FOMC meeting minutes revealed that Fed officials considered both rate maintenance and potential rate increase scenarios due to war-related inflation risks, particularly energy price pressures that could outweigh employment concerns. The Trump administration's protectionist trade policies, including Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum, and copper, continue shaping global trade dynamics while raising concerns about retaliatory measures from trading partners.
sections.AI & Economy: Goldman Sachs research indicates that AI-driven labor displacement could increase unemployment rates by up to 0.5 percentage points over the next decade, with affected workers experiencing approximately 10 percentage point wage reductions upon reemployment. Alibaba announced a major AI data center project in Guangdong province in collaboration with China Telecom, deploying approximately 10,000 custom-developed Zhenyu AI chips with potential expansion to 100,000 chips, positioning China to circumvent US semiconductor export restrictions. LG AI Research Institute unveiled its multimodal AI model ExaOne 4.5, capable of simultaneously processing text and images for industrial applications including contract analysis, technical drawings, and financial documents, demonstrating competitive STEM performance metrics and representing advancement in Korean independent foundation models.
sections.Others: The prolonged US-Iran conflict has created ripple effects throughout the Korean economy, affecting export-dependent businesses, job creation, and consumer confidence as reduced trade and supply chain disruptions threaten corporate profitability. Concerns about the ceasefire's durability persist as Israel conducted Lebanon airstrikes on the first day of the agreement causing approximately 1,000 casualties, with Iran signaling potential withdrawal from the deal if violations continue. Allegations of insider trading have emerged with reports of large futures contracts sold three hours before Trump's ceasefire announcement and purchased during the ensuing oil price decline of approximately 15%, raising questions about information asymmetry and market manipulation. The United Arab Emirates formally stated that Iran must cease terrorist attacks and guarantee freedom of navigation in the Hormuz Strait as preconditions for sustained peace.
